summary: Ludo Rocher was an Indology scholar who studied at Ghent University under Adriaan Scharpé, Jan Gonda, and Barend Faddegon, among others. He was a professor at Université libre de Bruxelles (1959–1967) and held a chair at the University of Pennsylvania (1966–2002).

Ludwig Alsdorf was an Indologist who studied at Hamburg under Walther Schubring and completed his habilitation at Berlin under Heinrich Lüders. His career included posts at Allahabad (1930–1932), Berlin (1935, 1944), and the University of Hamburg (1950–1972).

Ludwig Diestel was a religious studies scholar who studied under Heinrich Ewald (~1845–1848). He held academic posts at the universities of Bonn (~1858–1862), Greifswald (~1862–1867), Jena (~1867–1874), and Tübingen (~1874–1879).

Ludwig Heller was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Franz Kielhorn at the University of Göttingen (Dr. phil. 1887–1893) and Greifswald, later serving as an extraordinary professor at Greifswald (1904) and at the University of Tartu (1918).

Ludwig Lange was a scholar in linguistics and history. He studied at Leipzig and under Theodor Benfey at Göttingen, where he habilitated in 1843. He held professorships at Charles University (1853–1859), University of Giessen (1859), and University of Leipzig (1871).

Ludwig Ross was a historian and archaeologist who studied at Kiel University (~1825–1827). He served at the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (1837–1843) and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1845–1859).
Ludwig Timotheus Spittler was a historian who studied at the University of Tübingen (~1771–1775). He held an academic post at the University of Göttingen from ~1779 to 1797.

Ludwig Wittgenstein was a philosopher who studied at Technische Hochschule Berlin, the University of Manchester, and the University of Cambridge. He served as a fellow and lecturer at Trinity College (1929–1947) and professor of philosophy at Cambridge (1930–1947).
Ludwik Skurzak was an Indologist who studied under Stanisław Schayer. He served as a lecturer at the University of Breslau.
Luigi Suali was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Bologna and under Hermann Jacobi (~1904–1906). He held a post at the University of Pavia from ~1912 to 1937.

Luis O. Gómez was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Insler and later degrees at Michigan, serving as department chair and professor at Michigan (1986, 1997) and academic director at Mangalam Research Center (~2008–2017).

Luise Hercus was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She was a tutor and lecturer at St Anne's (1948–1954) and taught Sanskrit at the Australian National University (~1969–1991).

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery and studied under Horwa Drungrampa Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot beginning in 1969.

Luo Changpei was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Peking University (~1916–1921). He held positions at Northwest University (~1921–1926), Xiamen University (~1926–1927), Sun Yat-sen University (~1928–1929), and Peking University (~1934–1949).

Lutz Bieg is a sinologist who studied at Heidelberg University (Dr. phil. ~1963–1971) and Freie Universität Berlin (habilitation by 1986). He served as professor of Chinese literature and philosophy at the University of Cologne from 1989 to 2008.

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Lancaster University (BA, MA) and the University of Oxford (D. Phil 1987). She served as a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

Léon Feer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Philippe-Édouard Foucaux and Étienne Marc Quatremère, holding posts at the INALCO (chair of Tibetan from 1864), Collège de France (1869–1872), and Bibliothèque nationale de France (from 1872).

Léon Vandermeersch was a sinologist and philosopher educated at INALCO, the University of Paris, and EPHE. He held posts at Aix-Marseille (1966–1973), Paris Diderot (1973–1979), EPHE (1979–1993), and served as director of the EFEO (1989–1993).

Lê Mạnh Thát is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history. He studied at Saigon University (~1962–1965) and earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1965–1974), later holding a post at Van Hanh University (~1974–1975).
M. Athar Ali was a scholar of history and Indology who studied at Aligarh Muslim University from ~1948 to 1953, where he subsequently served as a historian from ~1953 to 1990.
